Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Do you need an induction? It may help to induce trance if you are sober, distracted, analytical, or otherwise not very trancey, as it is helpful to bring together your attention and make you more receptive to the quieter materials. You do not have to induce trance by having someone take over your will, making you fall asleep to play, or otherwise make you do something you don’t want to do. If you are already trancey from meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, etc., you can probably skip the induction and go straight to orientation and containment.

How much trance is enough? Enough trance for the practice to feel focused and warm, receptive and embodied, and for you to be able to stop the practice when you need to. Deeper trance may be useful, but it is not necessary.

What an induction is actually doing

It's preparation, gathering up attention. It may also be deepening. It will be more effective if you tailor it to what comes up. Counting is easy but you can do all sorts of things to gather up attention. It's OK to tell people when you're doing this rather than pretending it's all very elegant and flowing.

You may want to try your suggestion on a simple target before deepening to see if it works. It's not necessary to do the whole ceremony before responding more receptively.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Choose what you're going to do, one way to anchor it initially, and how you'll get back. You may want it to be warm, or firm, directed, or neutral, or whatever. You don't have to combine floating, going down stairs, going through gardens, visiting inner places, seeing a colour, and talking to a child all in one go, even if some of these appeal to you. If you do change metaphors do it consciously.

It's OK to do this with no imagery. The signal may come in other ways (feelings, rhythm, movement, words, spatial, knowing, or even non-response, if that's appropriate to the context). Try to keep the language you use for counting in and elsewhere consistent with the world you've chosen. Come back out by reversing the journey in some way. It's OK to steal qualities from other inductions but don't become someone else.

Try to limit yourself to one key verb, a particular sense quality, a short bit of text to repeat, and a way of moving from one bit to another. Read it out loud before hand - long beautiful sentences tend to turn to soup in inductions.

Before you begin

Read this induction and Come all the way back while awake. Consider what you want to explore, what you want to leave alone, and how long you've got. Try to use it for something good (e.g. more love, play, confidence, creativity, communion with life, whatever). Make sure you've got enough time to come back out and think about it.

Make sure you're somewhere safe - don't do this when driving, near water, playing with machinery, or with people who need looking after. Don't do this when intoxicated or in any other state where you may be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself. (However see the bit about already being open, later, as this is not about deepening when unstable).

Consider whether you want it to be encouraging, warm, firm, or whatever. You may want to warn yourself that your eyes will be asked to close and that you may come out and go in again a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you're listening to a recording it may be a good idea to read the script first (if possible). Decide on a word to use to come out (e.g. 'stop'). You may also want words to make it less demanding (e.g. 'less'), and to stop the words (e.g. 'quiet'). You can always just open your eyes and finish - you don't have to get consensus from inner parts to do this.

Until you are confident about how to get in and out, it is wise to rehearse the skill in a context where you do not require the maximum effort that difficult subjects demand. Once the skill is easier to apply, you can relax into using it effortlessly. It is the lack of effort that produces the maximum benefit. Saying no is enough. You don’t have to say anything.

Develop the next part of your induction from what your subject is responding to, not what you intended. This principle of utilization means that whatever happens can be developed. If nothing happens, then nothing has happened. You don’t have to pretend that something has. The subject needs to know they are safe and how to leave the experience. The language skills that facilitate these are described in Appendix B and used in Let the next response guide you .

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Fractionation is when you bring the person back up and send them back down into absorption. As long as you're doing it openly (telling them you're doing it), it's okay, because it teaches the person that they can always get out of trance. Not all questions should have the answer "deeper."

At some point you can say, "When you're ready, open your eyes and bring yourself all the way back up. You can decide if you want to end the hypnosis here, or you can close/soften your eyes and send yourself back down into absorption again."

Deepening, if useful

"When it's useful for me to deepen my absorption, I can. When it's not useful, I'm just as awake as I need to be."

Then you can do a room in your heart, or a garden, or a temple, or sitting next to a fire with your Protector nearby, or floating on a clear lake, or sitting in a chair, etc. Don't do more than one of these.

You're not going to make it happen or fake it. You're just going to wait with love for it to happen.

It doesn't mean that anything will happen, but if something happens with one of your fingers, or you feel some other bodily change, it doesn't necessarily mean that it's real, but it does mean that something is listening to you.

A shortcut back into hypnosis

Once you've learned some of the inductions on this website and also the bringing yourself all the way back down induction, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. He even did it while driving, so don't use the same thing for calming yourself while driving as you do for going into inward hypnosis!

Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. When you are in a familiar and welcome hypnotic state that you like - not at the height of an emotional experience, and not in a child state or with a traumatic scene - start to pair that state with that word, phrase or gesture. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you will find yourself in that familiar and welcome state, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.

Return Fully When at another appropriate time you want to deliberately start practicing hypnosis, use your short cut. You can start to make your longer induction shorter as you find that the short cut works, but if it doesn't work, you can always use the familiar induction. There is no set number of times that you need to do this, or that you need to be instantaneously really deep into hypnosis or experience a particular sensation, it is completely up to you.

First, is it useful? Will it be there when you want it to be, not there when you don't want it to be? Can you change your mind about it and get back when you want to? It shouldn't mean you'll do anything you're told, anytime someone tells you, or even if you hear it overheard. Being able to go in faster should not limit what you can work with.

It's not a good idea to do it while driving or anything where you need to be actively paying attention even if it is open eyed and even if the words are conditional.

When you don't want it any more, stop practicing, take it out of any recordings or active apps you're using, go back to a familiar induction and say you're done using it. If you have problems not being able to stop using it or not being able to come back from it easily, get qualified help. The trigger should only be for the next time you decide you want to do a session, it shouldn't keep you out of line today.

Appendix H: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens”

I’m going to come from a bit more experience here.

Sometimes, during self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, extreme grief, prayer, or a variety of other altered states of consciousness, you may encounter something you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, some other kind of dark intelligence, or even a terrifying archetype. Sometimes it comes as a voice. Sometimes as an image. But it is not a simple emotion, and not merely a younger part.

First and foremost, it doesn’t matter for the purposes of this guide whether they are literally demons or not. All that matters is what the best way of dealing with them is, in terms of what leaves you feeling the safest, clearest, most loving, most grounded, etc.

Start with the room, the body, and basic safety

So what do you do when a demon, or jinn, or other bad or intrusive entity shows up? The same thing you do first for anything else— you check in with the room, your body, and safety in general.

“If there is anything that can be integrated right now, you may come forward. But know that you can wait, and that you will not be able to come forward until you are something that can be integrated. Know also that I will always be here as an adult, and that my body will bring you to a place of safety.”

If you feel like you’re in danger of hurting yourself or others, if you feel like you’re going psychotic and afraid, if you feel like you won’t be able to sleep afterwards, if you feel extremely paranoid, if you have chest pain, if you feel like you’re going to have a seizure, if you feel like you’re too hot in a serious way, if you feel like you’ve taken too much of something, or if you feel like you just can’t function in the world anymore, then the self-hypnosis session is over. Go get some real-world help.

A response check, not a verdict about what it is

If not, then check in with yourself as to what will be the best response. Again, it doesn’t matter whether or not it’s literally a demon. Put your hand on your heart, if that feels

2. Internalize that you do not have to know what this is. Ask yourself if it would be appropriate to send it some warmth or if you need to place a boundary with it. Know that you are under no obligation to do whatever it is asking of you.

3. If you feel vulnerable, tightness in your throat, sadness, fear or you sense you need to protect yourself in some manner, bring in your Nurturer. If it continues to be hostile or you feel afraid, then do not continue to engage with it.

4. Again, you do not have to know where this is coming from. Ask yourself if this way of responding to it seems to be clearing it. It is ok to use a combination of love and boundaries to interact with it.

Do not fight from fear

My first thought is to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it I’m more powerful, argue with it, panic, be it, etc. I have seen different prayers, mantras, protections, banishing and exorcism forms that some people find useful. The problem is, if you fight from fear…

…it becomes the center of your attention and when you hate it, give it a hook in you, or fight it from pride or panic….

So the next time the enemy enters the room, simply say to it, “I see that there is no reason to hate or revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to obey the voice in my head or in another. I see that there is no need to defeat what I am experiencing. I choose instead to return my attention to my loving awareness.”

A bodily boundary: compassion present, door closed

Secondly, feel free to maintain a bodily boundary and say to the presence “while compassion is present, the door is closed.”

This is especially important if the presence feels in any way hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc. It doesn’t respect my boundaries. In this case, don’t approach it with soft sentimental love. Invite it in for tea. Approach it with love while maintaining a boundary.

Sit up, ground your feet, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back slightly, feel the boundary of the skin around your torso and simply say “While I recognize that there may be suffering here and I want all suffering to go back where it came from, the boundary of this skin is the boundary of an adult now. You don’t get to come in the house anymore.”

If it might be psychosis or destabilization

Thirdly, this exercise is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of hostile presences which responds to grounding and love. It is not meant for people who may be going psychotic or experiencing other forms of destabilization.

If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days, are unable to sleep or function normally, are hearing voices, feel like you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, are going manic, are unable to communicate normally, or feel like you can’t tell the difference between symbolic experience and normal reality, get help immediately. This is not something to deal with in hypnosis.

As a general rule, if doing this makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, keep doing it. If it makes you more Paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, non-relational, scared, and non-functional, don’t do it.

The cosmic-download humility test

Finally, some of these presences or shadow forces or grandiose parts may respond not just by trying to scare you, but by trying to give you a sense that you are special, or trying to “download cosmic info” into you, etc. You can simply say “Unless the info you have to download is going to help me do the dishes or clean my room, I don’t need it.”

In other words, the guidance has to help you do the dishes or clean your room in a more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, useful way.

Don’t become an entity hobbyist

Finally, I recognize that some of you may be tempted to become hobbyists in regard to demons, jinns, hostile presences, Unattached Burdens, etc. The truth is, they all basically respond the same way. It’s good to learn how to relate to them with love, and it’s good to make your mind harder to hook, but beyond that, I don’t really want you becoming hobbyists in this area.

Appendix J: A practical induction library

Practise: Preview, choose a purpose, decide to start. All ‘families’ can be light, eyes open or with no trance contact replacement. Monitor what happens (even if nothing seems to change) and decide on next action: move on, imagine, change sensory channel, remain still, stop the sequence etc. Always do a complete waking return from induction.

NB If you cannot ‘see’ any images vividly, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial relations, touch, movement, knowing etc.

Stretch and release

Focus on a feeling of support (and perhaps the position of one hand or foot). Either actually or in imagination stretch slightly and/or press into the support and then release. Notice any difference in feeling (even if nothing seems to change). Repeat this with no more than 3 areas of the body. Use the notion of ‘release’ to guide you through the sequence. Ask yourself where in your body (and/or voice) you need to stretch or release and what you need by way of support to do this. Then bring back normal movement and return.

Supported floating

Use only 1% more effort than it takes to simply rest your weight on the support, or use the same weight and pressure. Notice what happens. It may help to fractionate, spending more time on in-breaths in normal awareness, and on out-breaths focusing on the support. Tell yourself you're going to do this before you start. What can you hear now? Return to normal weight and firm contact as you choose.

Rhythmic breath or pulse

Try it with a natural rhythm; perhaps the rhythm of breathing or a slight hum in the throat. Try it with a more artificial rhythm, such as tapping a finger or listening to sounds outside. Even try it counting (silently) to yourself, or even with no rhythm at all. Say the words 'here, and here again' over and over, until suddenly, stop the rhythm. This will bring about its own rhythm, the first one that appears - do not try and make it blank. This might bring a bit more clarity to what word, feeling, need or action is coming up. Then go back to using a normal rhythm.

Unwinding object

A quick exercise for when you have several concerns going on. Visualise each one as a strand of yarn, or even better, have some by you to help. When you've placed them all, take a minute to look at them all (without changing them, though you could label them if needed, by saying a word or two). How many did you end up with? Now pick one that is important to do something about, put the others somewhere you can see them, and come back to this page.

Sensory journey

Listen to the sounds of the room you are currently in and feel your body. Now imagine yourself walking somewhere, where do you want to go? As you walk, listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings. What texture are the objects you pass? What landmarks do you see? Now that you've collected enough attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can directly speak to whoever/whatever it is you want to speak to. Or you can just cut straight to the chase if you want. Observe what you want to observe, just don't make it into a "what are they going to do to you?" kind of thing. When you're ready to finish, imagine walking back the way you came and close the space.

Gradual wave

Begin with the smallest area possible that is neutral. Sense the current condition and sense it radiating outward to the next area, which should still feel comfortable. Continue this, pausing and sensing in each new area, or continue with the original area, only. Sense what the body needs to feel better, without thinking of medical terms. Allow the image to fade, sense the whole body, the contact points, and repeat the process.

Care workshop

First get ready as if you were going to work with a patient. Time, place, tools and boundaries. When you invite them in, the signal, the feeling or the younger state to come as close as you want them to be. Be careful to not use language which makes you fragmented. Ask them what they need, wait and see if you want to reconnect with them. If not, rest and see again. If you have an adult part which can do this or borrow a function from someone else, speak to them. You decide the words, the pace and what you want to do. The goal is to be as good as you can and not erase your history. Finally, close as you would with a patient. Say that you are whole, an adult and come back.

Resource embodiment

Choose someone or something who has a characteristic you want to adopt. Close your eyes and imagine them. Now imagine yourself becoming them, standing, walking and talking like them, just 1% more, or if you are uncomfortable with this, simply observe them, but in either case be aware of how you now have more access to that quality. Notice what happens. Repeat a few times. Now think of a situation you want to use that characteristic in. Finally let go of the person/thing, but keep the characteristic, and say to yourself "I am me", and notice how you have increased access to the characteristic you wanted.

No-trance inner contact

Things to do in between: keep the eyes open, notice where the practice is taking place and on what day, notice the feet, read something, write something, notice that one is still relatively normally aware.

Invitation: choose a question and keep it in mind, do not specifically focus or narrow the awareness further.

Choice: do whatever comes to mind, answer the question or write it down, write that one does not know, rest, change the question, ask someone else, stop the practice, etc.

Autonomous signal: write anything that comes to mind, no interpretation.

Deepener: none, it is not necessary to reach a state that is less alert.

Other autonomous: have the adult part of yourself answer the question in any way, preferably in writing or by taking an action.

Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous signal and take an action based on that, end the practice (no special exit is needed since no state was achieved that one needs to exit from).

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

You don’t have to know the terms to use the system. If you want to brush up on the art of imagery, how imagery is linked to bodily states, how to effectively rehearse new behaviors, how to choose more effective sentences to say to yourself, etc., then you might want to read this appendix. If you don’t know a little bit about NLP, it’s easy to turn NLP into a bag of tricks and forget that love, truth, contact, and consent are essential.

The four NLP layers

When it works, it works on a Sensory Level of NLP: changing where people see or hear an image, the distance or size or brightness, the volume of a sound, the posture of a remembered person, the pressure of an unpleasant sensation.

Second, it works on a State Level of NLP: helping them to access warmth, or a feeling of adult-ness, or courage, or steadiness, or love, or clarity.

Third, it works on a Strategy level of NLP: helping people to practice a new strategy.

Fourth, it works on a Language Level of NLP: pacing what is there, opening up people’s awareness, presuming their ability to do something safe, linking cause and effect in new ways, embedding suggestions, or asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative, or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

It's called the Milton Model and has to do with the architecture of the sentence. When I say "Relax now", or "Stop being anxious", or even "Trust me" a part of me braces against it.

The idea is to use indirect language to get past the part that wants to argue with me, and get to the place I want to go to.

To do that, I start with something I know to be true, and I take the pressure off by presuming the least possible capacity in the person and invite just one movement:

"As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone."

That way I pace reality, I open up awareness, I validate the function of what I'm doing, I presuppose the capacity to do what I want, I use a bridge to make the link easier, I invite only one small movement, and I have a way of testing with the body if it's happening.

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

To ‘Milton Model’ is to open things up. To ‘Meta Model’ is to ask “What do yo mean by that?” In order to be truly effective (and ethical) with people, it is necessary to do both.

“What do yo mean ‘Specifically’? According to who? ‘Good’ compared to what? ‘Always’? ‘Never’? What specifically would happen? How do yo know? What would constitute proof for ya?”

If, in session, it feels like the body is stiffening up, ‘Milton’ it. If it feels like truth is eluding ya, ‘Meta’ it.

To get back into a hypnotic state easily don't go for a peak emotional state but find a good receptive state that you can use. See the main induction section on a shortcut back into hypnosis. Make sure that this is separate from the alert, calming, synchronicity wake up thing.

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Sometimes when my clients notice a synchronicity they are asking straight way what it means. Sometimes it does give them a very good insight, sometimes it gives them a reason to start obsessing and look for patterns in everything. I am using noticing a synchronicity in a different way. I am using it as a signal to WAKE UP.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice a synchronicity, I use it to wake up in whatever state I am in at that moment, feel my body, the room I am in and go to the highest state I can where I can objectively and clearly see the situation I am in from the highest possible perspective, feeling my body and being still within the human reality. From this place I feel whatever feelings, search for the truth of the situation, and if I am in a negative state, I check if there is a message of my Inner Child, Protector, if I need to go through some grieving, if there is a message of my physical body about some problem that needs solving, or if there is a need for me to take some action in this situation. From this place of clarity and peace I am free to choose what to do next and usually I can do at least one thing that comes from a loving place. In this state I am also free and joyful and I feel grateful.

In short it is my cue to: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

It enables me to not get into identification, but still hear the message of the state if it is a negative one.

Installing the synchronicity cue

Mentally rehearse: when next synchronicity noticed (even harmless ones count),

feel 'whoa' as attention stimulated,

feel feet/body/breath/room to stimulate re-embodiment,

reiterate to yourself "when I notice synchronicity, it is a bell to wake me up, not a message to heed",

optionally ask Nurturer/Protector/Leader their thoughts,

rehearse further steps to get a more grounded and wide view,

rehearse what additional action to take, and finally rehearse waking completely,

Mind the caveats : it must be self-authored, obviously under control, reversible, and restricted to just helping orientation. It must not be used for decision-making, intuition, inhibition, or otherwise be under someone else's control.

This is a kind of implementation intention , for which there is evidence of efficacy (a good starting point is this paper by Gollwitzer ). Note that this specific application of implementation intentions probably hasn't been studied.

Synchronicity cues, like any cue, run the risk of creating false positives because you are creating an association in your mind by rehearsing it (this is the same mechanism by which synchronicity cues work), and when you are absorbed and/or destabilized, your mind may look for that pattern and interpret it as present when it may not actually be. Research has shown that people that score highly on apophenia (the tendency to perceive meaningful patterns where none exists) also score highly on false positives for patterns that are not present, and also score highly on traits on the psychosis spectrum (Blain et al., Grant et al.).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are creating false positives (you find yourself compelled to scan your environment for them, you are unable to sleep, you are anxious, you feel that random events are occurring to communicate something to you specifically, you find yourself unable to tell if they are real or not, etc.), you should deactivate them.

You can do this by simply ceasing to rehearse them, and saying, while fully awake, “Synchronicity is no longer to be used as a cue, and I let it go.” Also remove it from your list of cues so that you stop rehearsing it.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

When I reframe something that is dishonest with myself in the process, I’m no better off than before, so I have to be honest when I reframe. To reframe in a helpful way is to ask myself a series of questions like: “What else could be true here?” or “What is this part trying to do for me?” or “How would my Nurturer reframe this?” or “How would my Protector reframe this?” or “How would my Leader reframe this?” and so on.

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

1. How do I feel about this from inside myself? 2. If I were inside of this other person (or tree, or dog or whatever is not-you), how might I feel? 3. If I were across the room watching this, what would I see? 4. From the universal heart, what might be true, loving, clear about boundaries, and good for everyone involved?

Yes, it’s possible to use these positions to let yourself off the hook. It’s also possible to use them to get off the hook! Use them to see the truth from more than one angle. They’re a great way to get out of a prison of perception.

Appendix A: How to ask the subconscious a useful question

The subconscious is not an AI language model, but there is a certain overlap in how you can structure your questions to it to get the most useful answers. Prompt engineering can be very useful if used to become more present, more honest, more loving and to get more information. But useless or dangerous if used to be more controlling.

For maximum precision, include these 7 elements in your prompt:

Role (who/what are you talking to?)

Context (what is the situation?)

Intention (what do you want to change?)

Constraint (what is safe?)

Output (how do you want the answer: as an image, phrase, body signal, memory, action, question, symbol, silence, rest…?)

Evaluation (how do you evaluate the answer: is it true? kind? timely? stabilizing? specific? testable?)

Iteration (revise the prompt based on real life feedback)

Always include a “safe” fallback. If you don’t do that, the analytical part of your mind might fabricate answers to fit your prompt. Here is one fallback:

If the system needs more time to process this, or if silence is the best and safest answer, then let the body go into a deeper state of comfortable rest. The prompt is considered successfully answered with peaceful silence.

Sometimes there is no answer because nothing is happening. Sometimes the answer is that it is not time yet, or that you need to rest, build capacity, or do whatever it is you are supposed to be doing.

Core prompts

Here are the core prompts that can be mixed and matched:

Clarity: Wise subconscious mind, show me what is true, kind and timely. If there is something I need to know that is too intense to integrate, please transfer it to my conscious mind in a safe way that I can integrate. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.

Resistance: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust me 1% more?

Inner child: What do you need me to know? What can I do for you?

Protector: What do you need me to do in the real world for you to feel safe?

Leader/Guru: What is the direction that will be in alignment with truth, love, life and all beings?

Intuition: Let the intuition give me a signal. Let the analytical mind decipher it. Let the body give me feedback on my deciphering. Let reality inform me whether my interpretation is correct or not.

How to distinguish intuition from inherited programming: Wise subconscious mind, dissolve all the programming from my previous family, religion, marketing, erotic imprints, political tribe, trauma responses, and need for belonging as a child. Show me how these show up so I can see that they are just programming. Let them dissolve, or at least let them step back, so that I can receive the true guidance from the universal heart that will make my life better in simple, ordinary ways.

Daydreaming: Show me if this daydream is useful and guiding me, or if it is a way of not dealing with my life. If it is the latter, let me deal with my life.

Anxiety: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust my adult self more?

Truth that is hidden from you: Please don’t show it to me. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.

Integration: What can I do in ordinary life to integrate this?

The prompt will tell your subconscious what you are looking for. The NLP will help you approach it in a way that will be safer. Use both.
